description: Server-side review queue for offline-queued cashier writes that the scheduler classified as needs_review. Owned by Sales Manager / System Manager — cashiers do not see or edit these rows. The cashier's local outbox keeps a tombstone for dependency-graph integrity (parent_offline_ids, shift_offline_id) until the row resolves here.

fields.description: UUID v4 stamped by the cashier device at enqueue time. Globally unique within this site. The doctype enforces uniqueness so a duplicate handoff is a no-op idempotent return.
fields.label: Offline ID

fields.description: Which outbox endpoint the entry was queued against. Mirrors the client's `OutboxType` taxonomy (see frontend/src/offline/types.ts) so round-tripping a row between cashier device and server keeps the type stable. Drives which `pospire.pospire.api.offline.*` method `recovery.retry` invokes on replay.
fields.label: Entry Type
fields.options:
invoice
customer
material_receipt
opening_entry
closing_entry
return

fields.description: State machine: Pending Review -> In Review -> Retrying -> Resolved or Voided. Retry failure transitions back to Pending Review with attempt_count incremented.
fields.label: Status
fields.options:
Pending Review
In Review
Retrying
Resolved
Voided

fields.description: The cashier user who originated the queued write. Replay impersonates this user via `_acting_as_user` so attribution stays with them — the manager is recorded separately as reviewer_user.
fields.label: Cashier

fields.description: Device identifier set at enqueue time. Useful for diagnosing device-specific failure clusters (e.g. a single iPad with a broken offer config).
fields.label: Device ID

fields.description: P-11: posting_date snapshotted at enqueue time. Replay uses this, NOT today.
fields.label: Posting Date

fields.description: offline_id of the POS Opening Shift this entry posts to. Required for invoices and closing entries — drives shift validation on replay.
fields.label: Shift Offline ID

fields.description: JSON array of offline_ids this entry depends on (e.g. closing depends on its sibling invoices). The local cashier outbox keeps tombstones until ALL parents resolve here, preserving the dependency graph.
fields.label: Parent Offline IDs (JSON)

fields.description: Build hash of the client that queued this entry. Lets ops correlate failures with a known-bad client version when a fleet-wide schema change rolls out.
fields.label: Client Build Hash

fields.description: Schema version of the queued payload. Bumped when the offline_id contract changes server-side; recovery.retry refuses to replay if the server's expected version doesn't match.
fields.label: Schema Version

fields.description: Stable category from the offline error taxonomy (`permission_error`, `accounting_period_closed`, `parent_not_ready`, `customer_missing`, etc). Drives the manager UI's per-category guidance.
fields.label: Error Category

fields.description: Attempts the scheduler made before classifying this entry as needs_review, plus any manager-driven retries here.
fields.label: Attempt Count

fields.description: Server-supplied error detail from the failing replay. Truncated to a sensible length to keep the row under MariaDB row-size limits; the full traceback is in Error Log keyed by offline_id.
fields.label: Error Detail

fields.description: Verbatim payload as the cashier device queued it. Immutable after handoff — this is the audit-grade record. If the manager ever needs to edit (phase 2), the working copy goes into `payload`; this field is never overwritten.
fields.label: Original Payload (immutable)

fields.description: sha256 of original_payload at handoff time. Tamper detection — if this doesn't match recompute(original_payload), something has rewritten the doctype row outside the supported flow.
fields.label: Original Payload Hash

fields.description: Working copy used by recovery.retry. Identical to original_payload at handoff; phase 2 may allow targeted edits here. Edits are tracked via Activity rows and require reviewer_notes.
fields.label: Working Payload

fields.description: sha256 of `payload`. If equal to original_payload_hash, the working copy hasn't been edited.
fields.label: Payload Hash

fields.description: Server doctype the resolved payload was inserted into (Sales Invoice, Customer, Stock Entry, etc). Populated when status transitions to Resolved.
fields.label: Resolved Doctype

fields.description: Resolved server document name. Dynamic Link target is `resolved_doctype` so this field can point to Sales Invoice, Customer, etc.
fields.label: Resolved Doc Name

fields.description: P2-22 — when checked, the daily auto-archive job (P2-27) will skip this row regardless of age or terminal status. Use for entries under audit / dispute / legal subpoena. Only System Manager can flip the flag.
fields.label: Legal Hold

fields.description: Manager who acted (retry/void). Distinct from cashier_user — recovery actions are attributed to the manager, the underlying transaction stays attributed to the cashier.
fields.label: Reviewer

fields.description: Free-form note required when voiding. Optional on retry.
fields.label: Reviewer Notes

fields.description: Required when legal_hold is checked — captures the reason (incident reference, audit case ID, dispute number) so the hold can be reconciled later. Stored verbatim; not redacted by archival.
fields.label: Legal Hold Reason

fields.description: Append-only audit trail. Every handoff, retry, void, and note action writes a row here. Rows are never edited or deleted.
fields.label: Activity

fields.description: Field-level edit history. Each manager-driven payload mutation writes one row per changed field with before/after values, the reviewer's reason, and editor identity. Distinct from Activity (action-level) — Edits describe WHAT changed inside the payload.
fields.label: Edit History

name: POSpire Offline Sync Review
